previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 68-year-old female with end-stage renal disease, atrial fibrillation, and insulin-dependent diabetes was admitted after developing bleeding at the site of a newly placed tunneled dialysis catheter. The catheter was placed via the right internal jugular vein following angioplasty for venous stenosis. She presented with minor oozing but remained hemodynamically stable, with no significant drop in hemoglobin. The bleeding resolved with continuous pressure dressings. Warfarin was held temporarily and later resumed. She completed a dialysis session without complications and was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to monitor the catheter site, restart anticoagulation, adhere to fluid and sodium restrictions, and resume her regular dialysis schedule.
